SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

FEB 14 1939

French Deny War
Aces Sent China

Japanese Report On 49
Pilots Declared
“Groundless”

(Havas)
PARIS, Feb. 13. — “Entirely groundless” is the report emanating from a Japanese source and announcing that 49 French airmen, divided into three groups, have gone or are going to China to assist the Chinese Government in the hostilities, official quarters here declared today.
The Japanese report in question alleged that Dr. Wellington Koo, Chinese Ambassador to France, had persuaded French fliers to “help in the reconstruction of Chinese air forces.”
An advance group of 18 men led by Lt.-Col. Laurent, World War ace and adviser to the Schneider Corporation, had assertedly left Marseilles late last year and were stated to be in active service now.
A second party of 16 men had allegedly departed from France in the middle of last month, while a third group of 15 airmen is to sail from Marseille; this coming Friday, the report added.
The Japanese despatch concluded in stating, “The French fliers reportedly have been recruited by M. Pierre Cot, former French Air Minister.
“By this move, further indications of French assistance to the National Government, in an effort to counteract Japanese gains in China, was seen by observers.”

《上海晚邮报与信使报》（SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY）

1939年2月14日

法国否认派遣
王牌飞行员赴华

日本关于49名
飞行员的报道被指
“毫无根据”

（哈瓦斯社）
巴黎，2月13日电。——当地官方人士今日宣称，来自日本方面并称49名法国飞行员已分三批前往或正前往中国协助中国政府作战的报道“完全毫无根据”。
该日本报道声称，中国驻法大使顾维钧博士已说服法国飞行员“帮助重建中国空军”。
报道断言，由第一次世界大战王牌飞行员、施耐德公司顾问洛朗中校（Lt.-Col. Laurent）率领的18人先遣队已于去年年底离开马赛，目前正处于现役状态。
报道还称，第二批16人已于上月中旬离开法国，而第三批15名飞行员将于本周五从马赛启航。
日本电文最后称：“据称，这些法国飞行员是由前法国空军部长皮埃尔·科特先生（M. Pierre Cot）招募的。”
“观察家认为，此举进一步表明法国正在援助国民政府，以抵消日本在中国取得的战果。”

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY

FEB 13 1938

French Airmen
Joining China
New Air Force

(Domei)
TOKYO, Feb. 13.—Forty-five
French fliers have been persuaded
by Dr. Wellington Koo, Chinese
Ambassador to France, to help
the reconstruction of Chinese Air
forces, according to information
received here today.
An advance party of 18, head-
ed by Lieut.-Col. Laurent, former
World War ace, and at present
adviser to the Schneider Corpora-
tion, sailed from Marseilles late
last year and are now working in
the front lines, the reports stated.
A second group of 16, which
left Marseilles about the middle
of January has just reached
China, while a third group of 13
is scheduled to sail from
Marseilles this Friday for China,
according to the reports.
The French fliers reportedly
have been recruited by M. Pierre
Cot, former French Air Minister.
By this move, further indication
of French assistance to the Kuo-
mintang regime in an effort to
counteract Japanese gains in
China, was seen by observers.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》

1938年2月13日

法国飞行员
加入中国
新空军

（同盟社）
东京，2月13日电。——据今日在此收到的消息，中国驻法大使顾维钧博士已说服45名法国飞行员帮助重建中国空军。
报道称，由前第一次世界大战王牌飞行员、现任施耐德公司顾问的洛朗中校（Lieut.-Col. Laurent）率领的18人先遣队已于去年年底从马赛启航，目前在前线服役。
另据报道，第二批16人约于1月中旬离开马赛，刚刚抵达中国；而第三批13人计划于本周五从马赛启航前往中国。
据称，这些法国飞行员是由前法国空军部长皮埃尔·科特先生（M. Pierre Cot）招募的。
观察家认为，此举进一步表明法国正在援助国民党政权，以抵消日本在中国取得的战果。

(14)

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

FEB 13 1939

Foreigners to Fly For
Chinese in South

More than 80 foreign aviators
arrived in Yunnan and Kwangsi
recently by way of Hongkong to
join the Chinese air force, a Hong-
kong dispatch reaching here yester-
day said.

Most of these foreign aviators are
of U.S. and Soviet nationalities, the
report said. With the exception of
a few who will serve as aviation in-
structors, the aviators will be em-
ployed by the Chinese to fly combat
planes, the despatch stated.

（批：3/2）

《字林西报》（NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS）

1939年2月13日

外国人将在华南
为中国人驾驶飞机

昨日到达此处的一份香港电讯称，最近有80多名外国飞行员经香港抵达云南和广西，加入中国空军。

报道指出，这些外国飞行员大多为美国和苏联国籍。电讯称，除少数人将担任航空教官外，其余飞行员将被中方雇用驾驶作战飞机。

（批注：3/2）

Date ____ 19____

Subject Chinese Air Force - Foreign recruit report published in the
Shanghai Evening News & Mercury dated January 13, 1939.

Made by J. S. Lockwood. Forwarded by C. Gamba J.

With reference to the report published by the
Shanghai Evening News & Mercury on January 13, 1939 regarding
the enlistment of foreign personnel in the Chinese Air Force,
enquiries from reliable sources show that a similar rumour
has been prevalent in local circles for the past few weeks,
but official confirmation is lacking.

The Chinese Air Force continues to receive supplies
and equipment from the Soviet. All aircraft, thus supplied,
are piloted and serviced by Soviet personnel. The larger
percentage of the Chinese Air Force is said to be under
the control of Soviet advisors to the Chinese Government.
Machines manufactured in Great Britain and the U. S. A.
are also used, but, as far as it can be ascertained, the
pilots are of Chinese nationality. The maintenance and
repair of aircraft is performed by Chinese mechanics
working under the supervision of foreign foremen.

J. S. Lockwood.
D. S.

日期 ____ 19____

主题：关于1939年1月13日《上海晚邮报与信使报》刊登的中国空军外籍人员招募报道。

制作人：J. S. Lockwood。转呈人：C. Gamba J.

关于1939年1月13日《上海晚邮报与信使报》刊登的关于中国空军招募外籍人员的报道，经向可靠来源查询，过去几周内本地各界虽流传类似谣言，但缺乏官方证实。

中国空军继续从苏联获得补给和装备。所有由此供应的飞机均由苏联人员驾驶和维护。据说，中国空军的较大部分处于苏联驻华政府顾问的控制之下。英国和美国制造的飞机也有使用，但据查，飞行员均为中国籍。飞机的维护和修理工作由中国技工在外籍领班的监督下进行。

J. S. Lockwood.
D. S.

（左侧批注：FILE / 372）
（左下角批注：FILE / P. A. 10 G (S. Br.) C. (Special Branch).）

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JAN 13 1939

500 Foreigners
Claimed Joining
China Air Force

Aces Reach Chungking
To Form New Unit
Against Japan

GROUP INCLUDES
300 SOVIET VETS

New Zealanders Arrive
From Spanish Front
For Service

Five hundred foreign aviators, many of them veterans of aerial combats and bombing operations, have joined the new Chinese air force, according to reports in circulation at Hongkong. Many other volunteers have applied to join the air force and Mr. Quo Tai-chi, Ambassador at London, and Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, Ambassador at Paris, are said to be considering their applications.

Three hundred of the foreign volunteers for the Chinese air force are said to be Soviet Russians while the rest are mostly British and French. Several American, Canadian, Australian and New Zealand pilots have also joined. Two of the New Zealanders, the reports continued, have only recently left the Spanish war scene. They have left for Chungking after a brief stay in Hongkong. One of them has a record of four planes shot down while fighting for the Spanish Republicans, it is said.

Separate Branch

The volunteers, it is believed, will fly a separate branch of the new Chinese air force, cooperating with the Chinese fliers, the ranks of which have been materially increased during the last few months. Many of them have been graduated from the Central Aviation Academy in Yunnan and they will join the Chinese veterans who have survived the 18 months of hostilities.

This will mark the second time since the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities that China has engaged large forces of foreign volunteers for aerial combats. Earlier last year, a formidable force of American and other foreign aviators under Colonel Vincent Schmidt combatted the Japanese aviators in numerous battles, including the historic combat over Hankow when a big Japanese squadron was practically wiped out. Colonel Schmidt is also believed to have headed the Chinese squadron which raided the Japanese base at Formosa. They quit following a dispute over the enumeration.

Chinese Planes Resume

Chinese warplanes have resumed activities recently in South China after a prolonged recess. It is reported that they again bombed Japanese naval concentrations at Bocca Tigris in Pearl River and distributed handbills at Tunghun and Sheklung on the Canton-Kowloon Railway asking the Chinese civilians to evacuate the city in view of the general offensive which the Chinese troops are launching.

Meanwhile efforts have been redoubled to equip the growing Chinese air force with a sufficient supply of fast aircraft. Negotiations are said to be going on in America for the purchase of 200 Bellanca bombers fitted to carry seven bombs each. A large quantity of Soviet pursuit planes is understood to be at the disposal of the Chinese government.

（手写批注：D. S. Lockwood / C 14）
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》

1939年1月13日

声称有500名外国人
加入中国空军

王牌飞行员抵达重庆
组建新部队
对抗日军

队伍包括
300名苏联老兵

新西兰人从西班牙前线抵达
准备服役

据在香港流传的报道，500名外国飞行员（其中许多人是空战和轰炸行动的老兵）已加入新的中国空军。还有许多志愿者申请加入空军，据悉驻伦敦大使郭泰祺先生和驻巴黎大使顾维钧博士正在考虑他们的申请。

据说，为中国空军志愿效力的外国人中，有300名是苏联人，其余大多为英国人和法国人。也有几名美国、加拿大、澳大利亚和新西兰飞行员加入。报道续称，其中有两名新西兰人最近才离开西班牙战场。他们在香港短暂停留后已前往重庆。据说，其中一人在为西班牙共和派作战期间曾创下击落四架敌机的记录。

独立分支

据信，这些志愿者将驾驶新中国空军的一个独立分支，与中国飞行员协同作战；在过去几个月里，中国飞行员的队伍已大幅扩充。他们中许多人已从云南中央航空学校毕业，并将加入在18个月的战事中幸存下来的中国老兵行列。

这标志着自中日战事爆发以来，中国第二次动用大批外国志愿者进行空战。去年早些时候，由文森特·施密特上校（Colonel Vincent Schmidt）率领的一支强大的美国及其他外国飞行员队伍，在多次战斗中与日本飞行员交战，其中包括汉口上空的历史性战役，当时一大队日本机群几乎被全歼。据信，施密特上校还曾率领中国中队袭击日本在台湾的基地。他们因报酬纠纷而离职。

中国飞机恢复活动

经过长期停歇后，中国军用飞机最近在华南恢复了活动。据报道，它们再次轰炸了珠江虎门（Bocca Tigris）的日本海军集结地，并在广九铁路上的东莞（Tunghun）和石龙（Sheklung）散发传单，鉴于中国军队正在发动全面攻势，要求中国平民撤离城市。

与此同时，各方加倍努力为日益壮大的中国空军配备充足的快速飞机。据悉，美国正在进行谈判，拟购买200架贝兰卡（Bellanca）轰炸机，每架可携带七枚炸弹。据了解，大量苏联驱逐机已供中国政府支配。

（手写批注：D. S. Lockwood / C 14）

SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 1 4 1939

Ex-Loyalist Ace In China
To Join Air Force

Some men are perfect gluttons for punishment, as some one or other remarked some time ago. They are exemplified by a New Zealand aviator who has just arrived in Hongkong and who is now trying to join the Chinese air force; he comes from Spain via Australia, with a record of about eight months with the Loyalist air force over Madrid. With him comes another New Zealander, also an aviator, who is hoping to earn his living here as well.

The two men are E. N. Griffiths and L. A. Willicombe. Mr. Griffiths is the gentleman from Spain and in his right shoulder is the mark of a Spanish Insurgent bullet, a souvenir of an aerial "dog fight."

Mr. Griffiths arrived in Spain about a fortnight after the war started and enlisted with a fighter unit at Madrid. For the next eight months, he was kept busy in the air, fighting off bombers and pursuit ships alike. He was officially credited with having brought down four rebel 'planes.

In a "dog-fight" one day a bullet wounded him severely in the shoulder, he retained control of the machine, however, and brought it safely back to the aerodrome. Subsequently, a convalescent, he went to New Zealand, on to America, back to New Zealand again, and now he is in China, anxious to be in the air once more.

Mr. Willicombe, who arrived in Hongkong with Mr. Griffiths in the s.s. Taiping on January 6, has not had any experience of the "real thing" as regards fighting in the air. He has, however, a good record in the New Zealand Air Force, where one of his specialities was "aerobatics." After leaving the New Zealand Air Force he, too, decided that a "ground job" was no place for him and so he joined Mr. Griffiths in the trip to China in an attempt to earn his living by his trade.

《上海泰晤士报》（SHANGHAI TIMES）

1939年1月14日

前保皇派王牌飞行员在华
欲加入空军

正如某人不久前所言，有些人简直是自讨苦吃的典型。一位刚抵达香港并正试图加入中国空军的新西兰飞行员便是例证；他经澳大利亚来自西班牙，曾在马德里上空为保皇派空军服役约八个月。与他同来的还有另一位新西兰飞行员，他也希望在此谋生。

这两人是 E. N. Griffiths 和 L. A. Willicombe。Griffiths 先生就是那位来自西班牙的绅士，他的右肩上留有一颗西班牙叛军子弹的伤痕，那是一场空中“狗斗”的纪念。

Griffiths 先生在战争爆发约两周后抵达西班牙，并在马德里加入了一支战斗机部队。在接下来的八个月里，他在空中忙碌不已，既要抵御轰炸机，又要对付驱逐机。官方记录显示他击落了四架叛军飞机。

有一天在一次“狗斗”中，一颗子弹严重击伤了他的肩膀，但他仍控制住飞机，并将其安全飞回机场。随后，他在康复期间去了新西兰，又去了美国，再回到新西兰，现在他来到了中国，渴望再次翱翔蓝天。

Willicombe 先生于1月6日与 Griffiths 先生一同乘坐“太平轮”（s.s. Taiping）抵达香港，在空中实战方面没有任何经验。然而，他在新西兰空军有着良好的履历，其专长之一是“特技飞行”。离开新西兰空军后，他也认为“地面工作”不适合他，于是与 Griffiths 先生结伴前往中国，试图靠自己的手艺谋生。

page_data.en:
819
“Foreign Legion” Head
Of Fliers Tells Reason
For Aiding China Army

Veteran Of Five Wars Leads Daredevil Raid
Parties On Japanese Positions In China;
Air Arm Said Seeing Unusual Activity

(United Press)
HANKOW, Feb. 25.—Veteran of five wars and with four months service with the Chinese Air Force behind him, Vincent Schmidt, American ace and chief of the Chinese Air Force “Foreign Legion”, told the United Press here today that he had joined the Chinese Air Force “because only our weaker brothers need help— it is nonsense to help the strong.”

Schmidt, who is credited with having led the spectacular Chinese air raid on Formosa last Wednesday, began combat flying with the Chinese Air Force in November, but had fought Japan in the air before during the Shanghai War of 1932.

Soldier Of Fortune
A bluff, strapping American, Schmidt has also seen service in the Great War, the Mexican Revolution, the Italo-Ethiopian War and the Spanish civil war.
He won the rank of “Bomber Chieftain” with the Nationalist forces in Spain and came to China last October as one of forty American and European volunteers to the Chinese Air Force. At present he heads all foreign volunteers in the Chinese Air Force with the exception of Russians and carries the title of “Commander of the 14th Squadron” which consists of American and European volunteers.
Schmidt, 40 years of age, 6 feet tall and weighing 220 pounds, is cheerful but uncommunicative regarding his activities with the Chinese Air Force since he has been instructed to maintain strict secrecy regarding operations of the air arm of China’s fighting forces.

Cannot Tell
“I know, but I cannot tell,” is his usual answer to friends who question him regarding raids planned or already completed by China’s air squadrons. The self-styled “professional bomber,” it is worthy of note, came under suspicion of being a foreign spy shortly after his arrival in Nanking last October when he was seen associating with a French woman believed to have been engaged in espionage activities. Central Government authorities were said to have warned the American ace, resulting in his dropping of his French female friend.
Regarding the Chinese raid on Formosa and the possibility of expanded operations by the Chinese Air Force, including rumors of a planned raid on Japan proper, Schmidt today maintained his customary silence.

Noon Raids Disliked
Schmidt resides in the same building in which the United Press office is located here and eats at the Navy Y.M.C.A. He has an intense dislike for Japanese air raids at noon-time which force him to desert his tiffin for the cockpit of a Chinese pursuit plane. He says the past four weeks have been the busiest of his life because of frequent Chinese raids on Japanese positions along the Hwai River on the southern Tsinpu Railway and other raids on Nanking and Wuhu.
The American volunteer usually arises at 5 o’clock in the morning, not returning until dusk except for tiffin at the Navy Y.M.C.A. Each night he returns tired, apparently after a long flight to bomb some Japanese objective.

Narrow Escape
Schmidt’s most recent narrow escape was during a Chinese raid on Pengpu where the Japanese were understood to have had no anti-aircraft batteries. Schmidt dove down on the Japanese positions to drop his bombs, but suddenly found himself in the midst of a hail of tracer anti-aircraft bullets, three of which punctured his plane. Suddenly pulling out of the dive, Schmidt succeeded in escaping without being wounded.
Schmidt, unlike most foreign volunteers here, leads a quiet life, spending most of his evenings studying war maps of the next day’s objectives.
He is well aware of the American law against volunteering in foreign wars, but thus far has not been warned by American authorities here who say “Officially we do not know of Schmidt’s presence in Hankow.” Schmidt regards Mr. Nelson T. Johnson, American Ambassador to China, as an old friend and has told his friends that he regrets not being able to call on Mr. Johnson because of the possible legal complications.

D.S. 4/5
page_data.zh:
819
“外籍军团”飞行队首领
讲述援助中国军队的缘由

身经五次战争的老兵率领敢死队突袭
在华日军阵地；
据称空军观察到异常活动

（合众社）
汉口，2月25日电。——身经五次战争、并在中国空军服役四个月之久的美国王牌飞行员、中国空军“外籍军团”首领文森特·施密特（Vincent Schmidt）今日在此间向合众社表示，他加入中国空军是“因为只有较弱的兄弟才需要帮助——帮助强者是无稽之谈。”

施密特被认为于上周三领导了对台湾的精彩空袭，他于去年11月开始随中国空军参加战斗飞行，但在1932年上海战争期间，他曾在空中与日军交战。

职业军人
施密特是一位性格直率、体格健壮的美国人，他还曾参加过第一次世界大战、墨西哥革命、意埃战争和西班牙内战。
他在西班牙国民军部队中赢得了“轰炸机首领”的军衔，并于去年10月作为四十名加入中国空军的美国和欧洲志愿者之一来到中国。目前，除俄罗斯人外，他统领中国空军中的所有外国志愿者，并拥有由美国和欧洲志愿者组成的“第14中队指挥官”头衔。
现年40岁、身高6英尺、体重220磅的施密特性格开朗，但对中国空军的活动守口如瓶，因为他已接到指令，必须对中国作战部队空军的行动严格保密。

无可奉告
“我知道，但我不能说，”这是他对询问有关中国空军中队计划中或已完成的空袭的朋友们的惯常回答。值得注意的是，这位自称为“职业轰炸手”的人在去年10月抵达南京后不久便因涉嫌为外国间谍而受到怀疑，当时有人看见他与一名据信从事间谍活动的法国女子交往。据说中央政府当局警告了这位美国王牌飞行员，导致他断绝了与这位法国女友的关系。
关于中国对台湾的空袭以及中国空军扩大行动的可能性，包括有关计划空袭日本本土的传闻，施密特今天保持了他惯有的沉默。

不喜正午空袭
施密特居住在合众社办事处所在的同一栋大楼里，并在海军青年会用餐。他极度厌恶日军的正午空袭，这迫使他放弃午餐，钻进中国驱逐机的驾驶舱。他说，过去四周是他一生中最忙碌的时期，因为中国军队频繁空袭津浦铁路南段淮河沿线的日军阵地，以及对南京和芜湖的其他空袭。
这位美国志愿者通常清晨5点起床，除了去海军青年会用午餐外，直到黄昏才回来。每晚他都疲惫地归来，显然是在长途飞行轰炸某个日军目标之后。

死里逃生
施密特最近一次死里逃生的经历发生在中国军队空袭蚌埠期间，据悉当时日军在那里没有高射炮阵地。施密特俯冲向日军阵地投掷炸弹，但突然发现自己处于高射曳光弹的冰雹之中，其中三发子弹击穿了他的飞机。施密特突然拉起飞机脱离俯冲，成功逃脱且未受伤。
与这里的大多数外国志愿者不同，施密特过着安静的生活，大部分晚上都在研究第二天目标的作战地图。
他深知美国法律禁止志愿参加外国战争，但迄今为止，驻此间的美国当局并未向他提出警告，他们称：“官方上我们不知道施密特身在汉口。”施密特将美国驻华大使纳尔逊·T·约翰逊（Nelson T. Johnson）先生视为老朋友，并告诉朋友们，由于可能涉及法律纠纷，他遗憾无法拜访约翰逊先生。

D.S. 4/5

page_data.en:
The Aerial Foreign Legion Passes
DEMOBILIZATION of China's "foreign legion" of the air force has been announced from Hankow, but the announcement tells only half the story.
The group which is being demobilized, or rather reorganized, comprises only the 14th Bombardment Squadron of eight foreign pilots not including any Russians. The Soviet pilots, numbering not less than 40 and with their numbers increasing, will continue as a separate force although this fact is not stated in the announcement.
There are good men in the small foreign group of Americans, French, British, Australian and Canadian nationalities under leadership of Vincent Schmidt, veteran of Spain campaigns, now reported dismissed. But there has also been plenty of trouble—three Americans, picked by Chinese in the United States, having proved never to have been in an airplane before and to have faked their qualifications in order to get a free ride to China. For some time it has been clear that the Chinese air force would have to specialize either more or less in this matter of foreign pilots not of Soviet Russian nationality, and a variety of reasons made it appear advisable to let the dwindling group disintegrate completely. Now the remaining eight will go to other squadrons or to service as instructors.
The official statement announcing this action says that the "foreign legion" participated in aerial engagements with Japanese aircraft at Nanchang and Hankow and also in the bombing of Japanese positions on the Tientsin-Pukow railway front. Probably most of the publicity given these men has been overdrawn but it is certain that they have afforded valuable service to the Chinese cause and will prove of further assistance under the reorganization plan.
As to the Russians, they remain a very mysterious group—taciturn, and operating under strict orders not to let anyone inspect their planes while on the ground or learn much about them. At the beginning they seemed no great bargain at any price. There were many field crashes in landing their fast planes on rough terrain of inadequate dimensions, and their behaviour on raids was as mysterious as everything else about them. Talk persists that they caused the loss of a considerable number of other planes by calmly flying off while they were at a commanding altitude in a crucial moment. It is also persistently rumored that the National Government's control over these pilots is little more than nominal and that they fly if, when and where they choose; yet on the other hand high Government leaders assert their fundamental control over the Soviet pilots, and certainly it is Hankow which is paying their salaries.

The question of material supply certainly must figure largely in the general problem of China's military aircraft and personnel. No one else is giving as favorable terms for plane purchase as is the U.S.S.R. Ten-year credits are said to have been accorded. The pilots more or less go with the planes, it would appear. And indications are that both planes and pilots are in general giving satisfaction; meeting the canny Chinese requirement of a good deal for the money, in short.
Twin-engined bombers of high speed (so high as not to require pursuit-plane escort, it is rumored) and reasonably fast, highly maneuverable biplanes are Russia's great contributions in the way of material. The ultra-fast but poorly maneuverable monoplanes did not work out and there will be no more of them sent in. How much the Russians are doing for Chinese pilots in the way of training, or allowing them to fly Russian craft, is problematical. But the Chinese are receiving training in other quarters and they are getting more airplanes. With Dr. T.V. Soong now in a major aeronautic role, there will be better co-ordination and general improvement, including better provision in the way of air fields—long China's great need, and inexcusably neglected in the past.

（批：Zie [签名]）
page_data.zh:
空中外籍军团成为过去
汉口方面宣布解散中国空军的“外籍军团”，但这一声明只说了一半的事实。
正在解散，或者更确切地说是重组的群体，仅包括由八名非俄罗斯籍外国飞行员组成的第14轰炸机中队。苏联飞行员人数不少于40人，且数量还在增加，他们将作为一支独立的部队继续存在，尽管声明中并未提及这一事实。
在文森特·施密特领导的这支由美国人、法国人、英国人、澳大利亚人和加拿大人组成的小型外国团体中，不乏优秀人员。施密特是西班牙战役的老兵，据报道已被解职。但也出现了不少麻烦——三名由中国人在美国挑选的美国人，结果证明此前从未坐过飞机，为了获得免费前往中国的机会而伪造了资历。一段时间以来，很明显中国空军必须在非苏俄籍外国飞行员的问题上进行或多或少的专业化调整，各种理由使得让这一日益缩小的群体彻底瓦解显得更为可取。现在，剩下的八人将调往其他中队或担任教官。
宣布这一行动的官方声明称，“外籍军团”参与了南昌和汉口上空与日本飞机的空战，以及在津浦铁路前线轰炸日军阵地的行动。也许给予这些人的大部分宣传有些夸大，但可以肯定的是，他们为中国事业提供了宝贵的服务，并将在重组计划下提供进一步的协助。
至于俄罗斯人，他们仍然是一个非常神秘的群体——沉默寡言，并在严格的命令下行动，不允许任何人在地面检查他们的飞机或过多了解其情况。起初，他们似乎无论付出什么代价都不怎么划算。在尺寸不足且地形粗糙的地面上降落他们的快速飞机时，发生了许多野外坠毁事故，他们在空袭中的表现也像关于他们的其他事情一样神秘。一直有说法称，他们在关键时刻处于优势高度时冷静地飞离，导致其他相当数量的飞机损失。还一直有谣言称，国民政府对这些飞行员的控制几乎只是名义上的，他们随心所欲地在任何时间、任何地点飞行；然而另一方面，政府高层领导人坚称他们对苏联飞行员拥有根本性的控制权，而且确实是汉口在支付他们的薪水。

物资供应问题无疑在中国军用飞机和人员的总体问题中占据重要地位。没有其他国家像苏联那样提供如此优惠的飞机购买条件。据说给予了十年期的信贷。飞行员似乎是随着飞机一起提供的。迹象表明，无论是飞机还是飞行员，总体上令人满意；简而言之，符合精明的中国人对物有所值的要求。
高速双引擎轰炸机（据传速度之高以至于不需要驱逐机护航）以及速度适中、机动性极强的双翼机是俄罗斯在物资方面的主要贡献。超快但机动性差的单翼机效果不佳，将不再运送此类飞机。俄罗斯人在培训中国飞行员或允许他们驾驶俄罗斯飞机方面做了多少工作，尚存疑问。但中国人在其他地方接受培训，并且正在获得更多的飞机。随着宋子文博士现在在航空领域扮演重要角色，协调性和整体状况将得到改善，包括更好地提供机场设施——这长期以来是中国的一大需求，而在过去却被不可原谅地忽视了。

（批：Zie [签名]）

SECRET
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch - S.1 Station,
REPORT
Date November 4, 1937.
Subject Arrival in Shanghai of three French aviators seeking employment
in the Chinese Air Force.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by
Among the passengers arriving in Shanghai on the
Messageries Maritimes s.s. "Felix Roussel" on October 18,
1937 were the following three French aviators who embarked
at Marseilles:-
(1) Martial LAROCHE, aged 35.
(2) Marcel FLOREIN, aged 23 and
(3) Alfred PILAIN, aged 41.
All three have seen action as aviators on the Spanish
fronts, but whether they were fighting for the Republicans
or Nationalists is not known.
LAROCHE and FLOREIN, after arrival here, resided
at a boarding house situated at No. 390 Avenue Joffre
(Cafe Normandie), but left for Nanking on October 27 in
an effort to obtain positions with the Chinese Air Force.
PILAIN, who is accompanied by his wife, is at present
residing at Clements Apartments, 1363 Rue Lafayette, and
although it is known that he came to Shanghai with the
express intention of joining the Chinese Air Force, what
moves he has made to secure a post have not yet been learned.
According to reliable information PILAIN is an officer
on reserve of the French Army.
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH - 5 NOV 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）
Da. Pitts.
D. S.
D.C. (Special Branch).

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特别支部 - S.1 分站，
报告
日期：1937年11月4日。
主题：三名寻求在中国空军任职的法国飞行员抵达上海。
制作人：D.S. Pitts。转发人：
1937年10月18日，乘坐法国邮船公司轮船“费利克斯·鲁塞尔”号（s.s. "Felix Roussel"）抵达上海的乘客中，有以下三名从马赛登船的法国飞行员：-
(1) 马夏尔·拉罗什（Martial LAROCHE），35岁。
(2) 马塞尔·弗洛兰（Marcel FLOREIN），23岁，以及
(3) 阿尔弗雷德·皮兰（Alfred PILAIN），41岁。
三人均曾在西班牙战线作为飞行员参战，但不清楚他们是效力于共和派还是国民派。
拉罗什和弗洛兰抵达此处后，居住在霞飞路390号（诺曼底咖啡馆）的一处寄宿公寓，但于10月27日前往南京，试图在中国空军谋取职位。
皮兰由其妻子陪同，目前居住在拉斐特路1363号克莱门茨公寓（Clements Apartments），虽然已知他来上海是明确打算加入中国空军，但他为谋求职位采取了哪些行动，目前尚未获悉。
根据可靠消息，皮兰是法国陆军的预备役军官。
（印：特别支部 - 1937年11月5日 上海公共租界工部局警务处）
Da. Pitts.
D. S.
D.C. (特别支部)。

G. 47 M-1-36                                    File No. 51

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch - S.1. Station,
REPORT
Date October 28, 1937.

Subject Arrival in Shanghai of deserters from Italian forces in
Abyssinia desirous of joining the Chinese Air Force.

Made by D.S. Pitts.    Forwarded by C. Clausen D.S.

One Siro BELLUCI, Italian, born at Florence on August
11, 1911, a deserter from the Italian forces operating in
Abyssinia, arrived in Shanghai on the s.s. "Chenonceaux" as
a fourth-class passenger from Djibouti on September 22, 1937.
He was in possession of an Identity Card issued him by the
French Authorities in Djibouti. BELLUCI is now residing
at House No. 17, Passage No. 51 Route de Grouchy.

According to information received two other deserters
from the Italian Army also arrived in Shanghai on the same
steamer. The first, Alvero CINIGLIA, travelled as a 4th.
class passenger, whilst the second, Nando CATELLANI, was a
stowaway. After arrival here, CINIGLIA, who speaks
fluent French, proceeded to the French Consulate-General
on "business matters."

Soon after arrival here, BELLUCI and CATELLANI made
their way to the "LACI BAR" 7/9 Rue Chu Pao San in search
of employment. Through the good offices of Mr. Lazlo
BOCK, Hungarian, (he speaks excellent Italian), owner of
this establishment, BELLUCI was engaged as manager of the
"FANTASIO CABARET," located on Rue Chu Pao San, the proprietor
of which is a Mr. BARDELET, at a monthly salary of $80.00.

CINIGLIA and CATELLANI having had certain aviation
experience it is reported, endeavoured to obtain posts with
the Chinese Air Force, and in this connection it is believed
that CINIGLIA, who left this port for Hongkong on October 3,
1937 on the s.s. "Chenonceaux" is proceeding to Canton to
establish connection with the Chinese Forces in that city.

It is to be remarked that these three individuals all
harbour very pronounced anti-fascist sentiments.    D.S. Pitts.
D.C. (Special Branch).                                D.S.

G. 47 M-1-36                                    档案号 51

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特别支部 - S.1. 分站，
报告
日期：1937年10月28日。

主题：希望加入中国空军的意大利阿比西尼亚部队逃兵抵达上海。

制作人：D.S. Pitts。    转发人：C. Clausen D.S.

一名叫西罗·贝卢奇（Siro BELLUCI）的意大利人，1911年8月11日出生于佛罗伦萨，是从在阿比西尼亚作战的意大利部队中开小差的逃兵，于1937年9月22日作为四等舱乘客，乘坐轮船“谢农索”号（s.s. "Chenonceaux"）从吉布提抵达上海。他持有法国当局在吉布提签发给他的身份证。贝卢奇现居住在格劳西路（Route de Grouchy）51弄17号。

根据收到的消息，另外两名意大利军队逃兵也乘坐同一艘轮船抵达上海。第一名，阿尔韦罗·奇尼利亚（Alvero CINIGLIA），作为四等舱乘客旅行，而第二名，南多·卡特拉尼（Nando CATELLANI），则是偷渡者。抵达此处后，能说流利法语的奇尼利亚以“公务”为由前往法国总领事馆。

抵达此处后不久，贝卢奇和卡特拉尼前往朱葆三路7/9号的“LACI酒吧”寻找工作。通过该店店主、匈牙利人拉斯洛·博克（Lazlo BOCK）先生（他精通意大利语）的斡旋，贝卢奇被受雇为位于朱葆三路的“芬塔西奥歌舞厅”（FANTASIO CABARET）的经理，该店业主为巴尔德莱（BARDELET）先生，月薪80.00美元。

据报道，奇尼利亚和卡特拉尼具有一定的航空经验，试图在中国空军谋取职位，在此方面，据信奇尼利亚已于1937年10月3日乘坐轮船“谢农索”号离开本港前往香港，正前往广州与该市的中國军队建立联系。

值得注意的是，这三个人都怀有非常强烈的反法西斯情绪。    D.S. Pitts.
